newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe's comparative ads policy vague-German group.
newsitem.headline: Europe's comparative ads policy vague-German group.

text.p: Germany's central advertising association (ZAW) on Tuesday criticised the European Commission for failing to provide a clearer policy for what it called the grey area of comparative advertising law.

Referring to new directives the commission plans to submit to the European Union on comparative advertising, or ads that directly or indirectly contrast the attributes of companies' products or services, the ZAW said the plan was lacking.

"The Brussels project under the banner of 'liberalisation of comparative advertising' proves to be much ado about nothing," the ZAW said in a statement. "Incidents in the market will only be cleared up with expensive lawsuits."
The ZAW also accused Brussels of footdragging on implementing new policy, saying it could take three years before any decision on comparative advertising would be applied to the European market.

The countries of the EU currently have a wide range of policies on comparative advertising, ranging from the relatively liberal rules in Britain, Ireland, Austria and Switzerland to total bans in Italy and the Benelux countries.
Germany has no clear guidelines but allows courts to decide from case to case, the ZAW said.
